name: nonApi_checkReminders
description: Timer-triggered SP (RunCheckInNotification, every 1 minute; no parameters, no auth — internal to Azure Functions). Scans HC.Event (IsVisible = 1, deleted = 0, removed = 0) for runs inside the check-in window (EventStartDateTimeGmt within ±11 minutes of now, CheckInReminderSent NULL) or the RSVP window (±3 days + 1 minute, RsvpReminderSent NULL). Builds up to three messages per run: MessageType 1 'Time to check in', MessageType 2 'Time to RSVP', and — since 2026-10-03 (E5.F1.S10) — MessageType 3 'Get PackTrack ready' for every run in the check-in window. Only runs still in the future (minutesToEvent > 0) get a message. Returns two rowsets the C# trigger turns into FCM pushes (recipients are matched to messages on MessageId, because one run can now carry two messages), then stamps CheckInReminderSent / RsvpReminderSent on every run collected in step 1 so nothing is re-sent next tick. Recipients skip deleted hashers (Hasher.Removed = 1), removed kennel links, retired devices (Device.removed = 1), devices idle > 180 days (LastLogin) and NULL tokens; the UNION de-duplicates a token per message. A hasher who said RSVP Yes on an app build >= 1439 gets MessageType 3 instead of MessageType 1.

rowsets.name: MessageDetails
rowsets.description: One row per message (minutesToEvent > 0): type 1 and 3 for a run in the check-in window, type 2 for a run in the RSVP window. Empty when no reminders are due. Joined to HC.Hasher for the hardcoded HC system user (id 0CDBB109-…), so a missing system user would empty the rowset. MessageRelesabilityFlags keeps the HC5 typo so the C# EventMessage deserialiser still works.

columns.name: MessageId
columns.description: NEWID() per message — the key Rowset 1 joins on (one run can have a type 1 and a type 3 message).

columns.name: PublicEventId
columns.description: HC.Event.PublicEventId — public-facing event UUID for deep-links in push notifications.

columns.name: UserId
columns.description: HC.Hasher.PublicHasherId of the HC system user (looked up by internal id 0CDBB109-215E-4B5F-A405-F6C9FBCB18EC).

columns.name: UserDisplayName
columns.description: HC.Hasher.DisplayName for the HC system user. Computed column from Hasher table.

columns.name: UserPhoto
columns.description: HC.Hasher.Photo for the HC system user. Table column is NVARCHAR(1000) NULL.

columns.name: MessageTitle
columns.description: 'Time to check in' (1), 'Time to RSVP' (2) or 'Get PackTrack ready' (3).

columns.name: MessageContent
columns.description: Body text built from EventName and minutes/hours/days to start. Type 3: '"<run>" starts in N minutes. Tap to arm auto start: …'. NULL if EventName is NULL (string concatenation).

columns.name: MessageRelesabilityFlags
columns.description: Always 65535. Intentional typo in column name ('Relesability' not 'Releasability') preserved for C# EventMessage deserialiser compatibility.

columns.name: EventChatMessageCount
columns.description: Always 0. Obsolete since app version 2.1.3; kept for C# deserialiser compatibility.

columns.name: MessageType
columns.description: 1 = check-in reminder, 2 = RSVP reminder, 3 = 'get PackTrack ready' (opens Live Run, arms auto start, checks in at the start). Only sent to devices on build >= 1439; older apps read an unknown type as chat.

rowsets.name: Recipients
rowsets.description: UNION (distinct) of three branches. Type 1: kennel link with COALESCE(HEM.EventNotificationPreference, HKM.KennelNotificationPreference, 0) IN (1,3,4), device within 100 km of the run (GeoPoint, run SyncLatitude/SyncLongitude set), not checked in (AttendenceState < 20), and NOT (RSVP Yes on build >= 1439). Type 3: an HEM row with RsvpState = 3 or AttendenceState >= 20, not removed, preference COALESCE(NULLIF(HEM pref,0), HKM pref, 0) <> 2, build >= 1439, no distance fence. Type 2: preference IN (1,3,4) and no RSVP yet (RsvpState < 1), no fence. All branches: Hasher.Removed = 0, HKM.removed = 0, FcmToken NOT NULL, Device.removed = 0, Device.LastLogin within 180 days.

columns.name: UserId
columns.description: HC.HasherKennelMap.UserId — the recipient hasher's internal UUID.

columns.name: FcmToken
columns.description: HC.Device.FcmToken. Never NULL: every branch filters FcmToken IS NOT NULL.

columns.name: EventId
columns.description: The event this push relates to — links back to Rowset 0 EventId.

columns.name: MessageId
columns.description: #messages.id — matches Rowset 0 MessageId; the API matches recipients to messages on this.

sideEffects: Creates and drops temp tables #events and #messages.

UPDATE HC.Event SET CheckInReminderSent = GETDATE() (type-1 rows) / RsvpReminderSent = GETDATE() (type-2 rows) for EVERY run collected in step 1 — including runs whose start has already passed (minutesToEvent <= 0), which get no message but are stamped so they leave the window. Fires the Event updatedAt trigger, so stamped runs re-sync.
On stamp failure: INSERT HC.ErrorLog ('nonApi_checkReminders stamp failed') and continue — the rowsets are already returned, so the next tick may send a duplicate reminder.

codeSmells.issue: Rowsets are returned before the stamp UPDATE commits
codeSmells.detail: Steps 3 and 4 SELECT from #messages and return the rowsets, then Step 5 issues the UPDATE inside TRY/CATCH. If the timer trigger reads the rowsets and dispatches pushes before the stamp completes, and the stamp then fails, the next timer tick will re-process the same events and send duplicate reminders. This is documented as the preferred trade-off (duplicate reminder vs. lost push), but callers must be aware of the idempotency risk.

codeSmells.issue: SP body not wrapped in TRY/CATCH
codeSmells.detail: Only the stamp UPDATE (lines 265-283) is in TRY/CATCH. A runtime error in steps 1-4 (lines 55-259: temp tables, the GEOGRAPHY distance, the recipient UNION) reaches the RunCheckInNotification timer as a raw exception with NO HC.ErrorLog row — reminders silently stop for that tick (CLAUDE.md 'TRY/CATCH is mandatory on EVERY SP').

The HC system user id ('0CDBB109-215E-4B5F-A405-F6C9FBCB18EC') and PublicHasherId ('B6BAFD0D-5D2E-41CD-8495-811D551F01D0') are hardcoded literals. If these ever change in the DB, the SP breaks silently.
Column alias 'MessageRelesabilityFlags' (misspelling of 'Releasability') is intentionally preserved to avoid a C# breaking change. This is a known documented smell, not an accidental bug.

codeSmells.issue: Bare COALESCE on the notification preference (no NULLIF)
codeSmells.detail: COALESCE(hem.EventNotificationPreference, hkm.KennelNotificationPreference, 0) treats an event-level 0 ('no override') as the answer, so a hasher with the kennel switched on but an HEM row at 0 gets no reminder. Flagged 2026-09-25, not changed: fixing it would send MORE reminders, which is a product decision.

codeSmells.issue: Stamp CATCH logs without ErrorLog.id or userId and uses GETDATE()
codeSmells.detail: Lines 278-282 rely on the id column default (DF_ErrorLog_HasherId) and write HcVersion 'HC6'; the windows and stamps use server-local GETDATE() (lines 56, 74, 268) against EventStartDateTimeGmt. Azure SQL runs in UTC so it works, but SYSUTCDATETIME() would say what it means.
@minBuildPreRun = 1439 (line 49) gates MessageType 3 on TRY_CAST(Device.BuildNumber AS INT); a non-numeric BuildNumber silently counts as an old build.

breakingChanges: HC5 accepted an @apiKey parameter and validated it against a hardcoded key. HC6 removes @apiKey entirely — the timer trigger is internal to Azure Functions.
HC5 wrote a startup entry to LOG.GeneralLog. HC6 removes this noise (timer runs every minute).
HC5 stamp failure caused the SP to abort with a raw error. HC6 wraps the stamp in TRY/CATCH and continues — duplicate reminders are possible on transient stamp failures.
1.1.0 (2026-09-25): no rowset change. Recipients skip deleted hashers (Hasher.Removed = 1) and removed kennel links (HasherKennelMap.removed = 1).

1.2.0 (2026-10-03, E5.F1.S10): Rowset 0 can carry MessageType 3 'Get PackTrack ready'; Rowset 1 carries MessageId and callers must match recipients on it, not on EventId. Recipients also skip retired and 180-day-idle devices (2026-09-17).
